questions.s: Which of these is found in prokaryotic cells but not in eukaryotic cells?
questions.e: Prokaryotes have a nucleoid, a region of naked DNA without a nuclear envelope. Ribosomes (70S in prokaryotes), plasma membrane and cytoplasm occur in every cell type.

questions.s: Ribosomes are the site of
questions.e: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides. Lipid synthesis is mainly in smooth ER, and DNA replication occurs in the nucleus.

questions.s: Which pigment traps light energy in photosynthesis?
questions.e: Chlorophyll a is the main pigment that converts light energy into chemical energy in reaction centres. Haemoglobin carries oxygen and melanin colours skin.

questions.s: The monomer of a protein is a(n)
questions.e: Proteins are chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Nucleotides build nucleic acids and monosaccharides build carbohydrates.

questions.s: Which sugar is the main fuel normally oxidised in cellular respiration?
questions.e: Glucose enters glycolysis directly. Sucrose and lactose must first be hydrolysed, and ribose is a pentose found in RNA.

questions.s: Plant cells differ from animal cells in having
o: centrioles and a cellulose cell wall
a nucleus and many small vacuoles
ribosomes and a cell membrane only
questions.e: Chloroplasts and a large central vacuole are typical of plant cells. Both cell types have a nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes and a plasma membrane.

questions.s: Enzymes are biological catalysts. They work by
o: raising the temperature of the reaction mixture
being used up while the reaction proceeds
lowering the activation energy of a reaction
changing the final products of the reaction
questions.e: Enzymes provide an alternative pathway requiring less activation energy and are not consumed. They do not change the equilibrium or the nature of products.

questions.s: The movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential is called
questions.e: Osmosis is net water movement down a water potential gradient through a selectively permeable membrane. Active transport needs ATP and moves solutes.

questions.s: Which molecule is the universal energy currency of the cell?
questions.e: ATP releases usable energy when its terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed and is used by almost every energy-requiring process. NADH carries electrons, not directly used energy.

questions.s: Starch and glycogen are
o: proteins made of amino acid chains
lipids made of glycerol and acids
questions.e: Both are glucose polymers: starch stores energy in plants and glycogen in animals and fungi. Neither is a protein or a lipid.

questions.s: The fluid portion inside a chloroplast, where the Calvin cycle occurs, is the
questions.e: The stroma holds enzymes of the Calvin cycle. The matrix is the fluid of mitochondria and cristae are folds of the mitochondrial inner membrane.

questions.s: Which organelle is surrounded by a double membrane with pores called the nuclear envelope?
questions.e: The nucleus has a double-membrane envelope perforated by nuclear pores. Golgi complex, vacuoles and lysosomes are bounded by a single membrane or a stack of them.

questions.s: Vitamin B-complex and vitamin C are classified as
questions.e: B vitamins and vitamin C dissolve in water and are not stored much in the body. Vitamins A, D, E and K are the fat-soluble ones.

questions.s: The stage of cellular respiration that takes place in the cytoplasm is
questions.e: Glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate molecules in the cytosol. The other stages occur in mitochondria.

questions.s: Cellulose is digested by many herbivores only because their gut contains
o: their own cellulase from the liver
questions.e: Mammals cannot make cellulase; ruminants rely on symbiotic microbes. Salivary amylase digests starch, and bile emulsifies fat.

questions.s: Which of the following is a function of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.e: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and makes lipids and steroid hormones. Rough ER carries ribosomes, and ATP is mainly made in mitochondria.

questions.s: The two strands of a DNA double helix are held together by
questions.e: Complementary bases pair by hydrogen bonds: A with T by two and G with C by three. Peptide bonds and disulphide bridges belong to proteins.

questions.s: A cell in a hypotonic solution is most likely to
questions.e: A hypotonic solution has lower solute concentration than the cell, so water enters by osmosis. An animal cell may burst, whereas a plant cell becomes turgid.

questions.s: A plant cell placed in a concentrated salt solution undergoes plasmolysis. This means that
o: the cell swells and bursts open
the protoplast shrinks from the wall
the cell becomes firm and turgid
questions.e: Water leaves the vacuole and cytoplasm by osmosis, so the plasma membrane pulls away from the rigid wall. The wall stays intact.

questions.s: The sodium-potassium pump moves ions by
questions.e: The pump moves 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in against their gradients, using energy from ATP. Facilitated diffusion is passive and cannot move ions uphill.

questions.s: Which statement about the fluid mosaic model is correct?
o: Proteins form a continuous layer outside the lipids
Proteins float in a flexible phospholipid bilayer
The bilayer is rigid and its lipids never move
Phospholipid tails face outwards to the water
questions.e: In the model, the bilayer is fluid and proteins are embedded in it. The hydrophilic heads face the watery surroundings and the hydrophobic tails face inwards.

questions.s: In a competitive inhibition of an enzyme, the inhibitor
o: resembles the substrate and fits the active site
binds to a site away from the active site
increases the number of enzyme molecules
questions.e: A competitive inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site, and a higher substrate concentration reduces its effect. Binding at another site is non-competitive inhibition.

questions.s: Which of the following is a reducing sugar that gives a brick-red precipitate with Benedict's reagent on heating?
questions.e: Glucose has a free aldehyde group, so it reduces copper(II) to copper(I) oxide. Sucrose has no free reducing group, and polysaccharides give no reaction.

questions.s: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of
questions.e: Iodine fits inside the helix of amylose in starch and produces a blue-black colour. Proteins are tested with biuret reagent and fats with the emulsion test.

questions.s: A triglyceride is formed from
o: three glycerol and one fatty acid
one glycerol and two fatty acids with a phosphate
one glycerol and three fatty acids
three amino acids and one glycerol
questions.e: Three ester bonds join three fatty acids to glycerol. A phospholipid replaces one fatty acid with a phosphate-containing group.

questions.s: Saturated fatty acids differ from unsaturated ones in having
o: one or more carbon double bonds
a phosphate group in the chain
a branched amino group at one end
questions.e: Saturated chains carry the maximum number of hydrogen atoms and so contain only single bonds. Unsaturated chains have at least one C=C bond, which creates a kink.

questions.s: The secondary structure of a protein, such as the α-helix, is stabilised by
o: hydrogen bonds along the polypeptide backbone
hydrophobic interactions of the R groups only
questions.e: Hydrogen bonds between backbone C=O and N–H groups hold helices and pleated sheets. Peptide bonds form the primary structure, and R-group interactions shape the tertiary structure.

questions.s: Haemoglobin shows quaternary structure because it
o: is a single very long chain
has no prosthetic group at all
questions.e: Quaternary structure means more than one polypeptide assembled together; haemoglobin has two α and two β chains plus haem groups.

questions.s: Which base is present in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.e: RNA uses uracil in place of thymine. Adenine, guanine and cytosine occur in both nucleic acids.

questions.s: Which of the following is a pentose sugar found in DNA?
questions.e: DNA contains deoxyribose, which has one oxygen fewer than ribose at carbon 2. Glucose and fructose are hexoses.

questions.s: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place in the
questions.e: Photosystems and the electron transport chain are in the thylakoid membranes. The stroma is the site of the light-independent reactions.

questions.s: Oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.e: Photolysis of water at photosystem II releases electrons, protons and oxygen. Isotope experiments with labelled water confirm this origin.

questions.s: The enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide in the Calvin cycle is
questions.e: RuBisCO attaches CO₂ to ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP). Amylase digests starch and catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide.

questions.s: How many molecules of pyruvate are formed from one glucose molecule in glycolysis?
questions.e: The six-carbon glucose is split into two three-carbon pyruvate molecules, with a net gain of two ATP.

questions.s: In the absence of oxygen, yeast cells convert pyruvate into
questions.e: Alcoholic fermentation decarboxylates pyruvate to ethanal and then reduces it to ethanol, regenerating NAD⁺. Lactic acid fermentation occurs in muscle and some bacteria.

questions.s: Most of the ATP in aerobic respiration is produced by
o: oxidative phosphorylation on the inner membrane
substrate-level steps of the Krebs cycle
fermentation of pyruvate in the cytosol
questions.e: The electron transport chain and ATP synthase make about 26 to 28 ATP per glucose. Glycolysis and the Krebs cycle make only a few ATP directly.

questions.s: The final electron acceptor in the aerobic electron transport chain is
questions.e: Oxygen accepts electrons and protons to form water. Without it the chain stops, and NADH cannot be reoxidised.

questions.s: Which organelle is the site of protein modification, sorting and packaging for secretion?
questions.e: The Golgi complex modifies proteins received from the ER, for example adding sugar groups, and packages them into vesicles. Rough ER makes proteins but does not finally sort them.

questions.s: Cytoskeleton filaments that form spindle fibres during cell division are
questions.e: Microtubules made of tubulin form the spindle that separates chromosomes. Microfilaments are made of actin and help in cell movement.

questions.s: Which type of RNA carries the amino acids to the ribosome?
questions.e: Each transfer RNA brings a specific amino acid and matches its anticodon to the mRNA codon. mRNA carries the genetic message.

questions.s: The process in which large particles, such as bacteria, are engulfed by a cell is
questions.e: Phagocytosis is cell eating by pseudopodia, as in white blood cells. Pinocytosis takes in fluid droplets, and exocytosis releases material.

questions.s: A pea seed is soaked in water and swells because
o: active transport of water using ATP
evaporation of water from the seed coat
photosynthesis taking place in the cotyledons
questions.e: Imbibition is the absorption of water by hydrophilic colloids and needs no energy. Root-like active uptake does not occur in a dry seed.

questions.s: Why does an enzyme usually act on only one type of substrate?
o: It is much smaller than any substrate
Its active site has a fixed shape
It is made of lipids and not protein
It changes its shape in every reaction
questions.e: Specificity depends on the three-dimensional shape and chemistry of the active site, set by the protein's tertiary structure.

questions.s: Which structure of a mitochondrion increases the surface area for the electron transport chain?
questions.e: Folding of the inner membrane into cristae provides more space for carriers and ATP synthase. The matrix holds Krebs cycle enzymes.

questions.s: A student places red blood cells in 0.9 % saline and they keep their normal shape. This solution is
o: of higher water potential than the cell
questions.e: No net water movement occurs when the solution and cytoplasm have equal water potential, so the shape stays unchanged.

questions.s: A reaction catalysed by an enzyme has a rate that levels off even when more substrate is added. The most likely reason is that
o: the enzyme has been fully denatured
the product has become a new substrate
all the enzyme active sites are saturated
the activation energy has gone up sharply
questions.e: At high substrate concentration every active site is occupied, so the rate cannot rise until more enzyme is added. Denaturation would reduce the rate, not just level it.

questions.s: If the respiratory quotient (RQ) of a germinating seed is about 0.7, the respiratory substrate is mainly
questions.e: RQ is CO₂ produced divided by O₂ used. Fats need much oxygen to oxidise, giving about 0.7; carbohydrates give 1.0 and organic acids above 1.0.

questions.s: Net gain of ATP from glycolysis of one glucose molecule is
questions.e: Glycolysis uses 2 ATP in the investment phase and makes 4, so the net gain is 2. The figure 36 or 38 refers to the entire aerobic process.

questions.s: Which statement about Okazaki fragments is correct?
o: They form on the leading strand continuously
They are short DNA pieces on the lagging strand
They are RNA molecules that carry amino acids
They are made by RNA polymerase alone
questions.e: The lagging strand is synthesised in the 5′ to 3′ direction away from the fork in short fragments, later joined by DNA ligase.

questions.s: In the chemiosmotic theory, ATP synthase makes ATP using
o: the flow of protons down their gradient
direct transfer of phosphate from glucose
the flow of electrons through the enzyme itself
the splitting of water in the matrix space
questions.e: Electron transport pumps protons across the membrane; they flow back through ATP synthase and drive phosphorylation of ADP.

questions.s: The number of carbon atoms in the compound formed when acetyl CoA joins oxaloacetate in the Krebs cycle is
questions.e: Acetyl CoA gives two carbons and oxaloacetate has four, forming the six-carbon citrate.

questions.s: A DNA molecule of a bacterium has 20 % guanine. What is the percentage of adenine in this DNA?
questions.e: G = C = 20 %, so G + C = 40 %. The remaining 60 % is A + T, with A = T = 30 %.

questions.s: Which disaccharide is composed of glucose and galactose?
questions.e: Lactose, milk sugar, is galactose joined to glucose. Maltose is two glucose units, and sucrose is glucose with fructose.

questions.s: Which one of these pairs of molecules is correctly matched with its bond?
questions.e: A phosphodiester bond links the 3′ carbon of one nucleotide to the 5′ phosphate of the next. Glycosidic bonds link sugars and peptide bonds link amino acids.

questions.s: Which part of a phospholipid molecule is hydrophilic?
questions.e: The charged phosphate-containing head interacts with water, whereas the hydrocarbon tails avoid it and face the inside of the bilayer.

questions.s: Proteins are tested in the laboratory with biuret reagent, which gives a
questions.e: Biuret reagent turns violet where peptide bonds are present. Brick red is for reducing sugars with Benedict's reagent.

questions.s: Which of the following is the building block of cellulose?
questions.e: Cellulose chains consist of β-1,4 linked glucose units, which gives strong, straight fibres. Starch and glycogen use α-glucose.

questions.s: Which cell organelle contains its own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes?
questions.e: Chloroplasts and mitochondria have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic origin. Golgi, lysosomes and ER have no genome.

questions.s: Which statement about facilitated diffusion is correct?
o: It moves substances against the gradient
It requires hydrolysis of ATP to work
It uses carrier proteins but needs no ATP
It occurs only for water molecules
questions.e: Facilitated diffusion is passive: transport proteins help polar molecules and ions down their gradient. Only active transport moves uphill.

questions.s: The enzyme catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide into
questions.e: Catalase protects cells by converting toxic H₂O₂ into H₂O and O₂, producing bubbles when liver tissue is added to peroxide.

questions.s: Which organelle is known as the site of aerobic respiration in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.e: Krebs cycle enzymes lie in the mitochondrial matrix and the electron transport chain lies on the inner membrane, so most ATP is made there. Ribosomes make protein and lysosomes digest material; neither oxidises glucose.

questions.s: The cell wall of plants is made mainly of
questions.e: Plant cell walls consist chiefly of cellulose microfibrils. Chitin forms fungal walls and peptidoglycan forms bacterial walls; starch is a storage polysaccharide, not structural.

questions.s: Which organelle contains digestive enzymes that break down worn-out cell parts?
questions.e: Lysosomes hold hydrolytic enzymes working at acidic pH. Peroxisomes deal with hydrogen peroxide and fatty acid oxidation, not general digestion.

questions.s: Which bond joins two amino acids in a protein?
questions.e: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next. Glycosidic bonds link sugars, and phosphodiester bonds link nucleotides.

questions.s: As temperature rises well above the optimum for an enzyme, its activity falls because
o: the substrate molecules become too large
the activation energy of the reaction increases
the enzyme is denatured and its site changes
the enzyme turns into a new substrate
questions.e: High temperature breaks hydrogen and other weak bonds that hold the tertiary structure, so the active site no longer fits the substrate. Collisions are frequent but ineffective.

questions.s: The model of enzyme action in which the active site changes shape slightly on binding the substrate is the
questions.e: Induced fit says the active site is flexible and moulds around the substrate. In the lock and key model, the site is rigid and complementary from the start.

questions.s: Which products of the light-dependent reactions are used in the Calvin cycle?
questions.e: ATP supplies energy and NADPH supplies reducing power to fix carbon dioxide into sugar. Oxygen is released as a by-product, not used.

questions.s: The cell organelle that lacks a membrane is the
questions.e: Ribosomes are made of rRNA and protein with no membrane. Peroxisomes, vacuoles and chloroplasts are membrane-bound.

questions.s: Which feature distinguishes C₄ plants such as maize from C₃ plants?
o: They lack the Calvin cycle completely
They fix carbon without any chlorophyll
The first stable product is a four-carbon compound
They use only photosystem I and no ATP
questions.e: In C₄ plants, PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ into oxaloacetate in mesophyll cells, and the Calvin cycle occurs in bundle sheath cells. C₃ plants form a three-carbon compound first.

questions.s: A non-competitive inhibitor lowers the rate of an enzyme reaction. Adding more substrate
o: converts the inhibitor into a substrate
does not fully overcome the inhibition
questions.e: A non-competitive inhibitor binds to a site other than the active site and changes the enzyme's shape, so substrate cannot displace it.

questions.s: The scientific name of an organism is written in the form of a binomial. The two parts are the
questions.e: Binomial nomenclature, introduced by Linnaeus, names an organism by its genus (capital letter) and species (small letter), for example Homo sapiens.

questions.s: Who is known as the father of modern taxonomy?
questions.e: Linnaeus set up the hierarchy of classification and binomial naming. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom system, Darwin proposed natural selection, and Mendel studied inheritance.

questions.s: In the five-kingdom system of Whittaker, bacteria belong to the kingdom
questions.e: Prokaryotes such as bacteria and cyanobacteria are placed in Monera. Protista holds unicellular eukaryotes.

questions.s: Which taxonomic rank is the largest group in the hierarchy below kingdom?
questions.e: The order of ranks is kingdom, phylum (division in plants), class, order, family, genus, species. A phylum is the largest rank under the kingdom.

questions.s: Viruses are not classified in any of the five kingdoms mainly because they
o: are too small to ever be seen
are acellular and need a host to multiply
questions.e: A virus has a nucleic acid core in a protein coat, with no cytoplasm or metabolism of its own. Viruses do contain DNA or RNA.

questions.s: Which of these is a fungus?
questions.e: Yeast is a unicellular fungus. Amoeba and Euglena are protists, and Spirogyra is a green alga.

questions.s: Mushrooms obtain their food by
questions.e: Most fungi are saprotrophs: they secrete enzymes onto dead matter and absorb the digested products. They have no chlorophyll.

questions.s: The body of an earthworm is divided into many similar segments. It belongs to the phylum
questions.e: Annelids have a body divided into rings, and earthworms and leeches are examples. Nematodes are unsegmented roundworms.

questions.s: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.e: A bat has hair, mammary glands and gives birth to live young. A penguin is a bird, and a crocodile is a reptile.

questions.s: The tapeworm belongs to the phylum
questions.e: Tapeworms are flat, ribbon-like parasitic worms. Annelids are segmented worms and cnidarians include Hydra.

questions.s: Which of these is a producer in an ecosystem?
questions.e: Producers make organic food from carbon dioxide and water by photosynthesis. Rabbits and lions are consumers and mushrooms are decomposers.

questions.s: The ultimate source of energy for almost all ecosystems is the
questions.e: Producers capture solar energy by photosynthesis and it flows through the food chain. Soil and water provide materials, not energy input.

questions.s: A flowering plant whose seeds have two cotyledons is called a
questions.e: Dicots have two seed leaves, net-veined leaves and taproots. Monocots like wheat and maize have one cotyledon.

questions.s: Which of the following is a monocot plant?
questions.e: Wheat has one cotyledon, parallel leaf venation and fibrous roots. Mustard, gram and mango are dicots.

questions.s: Which group of plants has no vascular tissue?
questions.e: Mosses and liverworts lack xylem and phloem, so they stay small and live in damp places. Ferns, conifers and flowering plants have vascular tissue.

questions.s: Bacteria that live on the roots of legumes and convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia are
questions.e: Rhizobium forms root nodules and fixes nitrogen in symbiosis with legumes such as gram and peas.

questions.s: A group of individuals of the same species living in one area is a
questions.e: A population is one species in one place. A community includes all the populations, and an ecosystem adds the physical environment.

questions.s: Organisms that break down dead remains and return minerals to the soil are
questions.e: Bacteria and fungi decompose dead organisms and release nutrients for plants, completing the cycle of materials.

questions.s: The fish, frog, lizard, bird and rabbit all belong to the phylum
questions.e: All have a notochord at some stage, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and gill slits at some stage. They are vertebrates within Chordata.

questions.s: A frog lays its eggs in water and its larva breathes with gills. Frogs belong to the class
questions.e: Amphibians have a larval stage in water and moist skin as adults. Reptiles have dry scaly skin and lay eggs on land.

questions.s: The greenhouse effect is mainly increased by the gas
questions.e: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, and burning fossil fuels increases its level. Oxygen, nitrogen and argon do not absorb outgoing heat strongly.

questions.s: Bacteria that are spherical in shape are called
questions.e: Cocci are spherical, bacilli are rod-shaped, spirilla are spiral and vibrios are comma-shaped.

questions.s: Which structure distinguishes gymnosperms from angiosperms?
o: Presence of vessels and sieve tubes
Seeds not enclosed in an ovary
questions.e: Gymnosperms like pine bear seeds on cones with no fruit. Angiosperms enclose their seeds in an ovary that becomes a fruit.

questions.s: Double fertilisation is a characteristic feature of
questions.e: In angiosperms, one male gamete fuses with the egg and the other with the two polar nuclei to form triploid endosperm.

questions.s: The sporophyte is the dominant generation in
questions.e: In ferns the large leafy plant is the diploid sporophyte, and the gametophyte is a small prothallus. In mosses the gametophyte dominates.

questions.s: Which one of these is an example of Cnidaria?
questions.e: Cnidarians have stinging cells (cnidocytes) and a radial body with two cell layers. Starfish are echinoderms and octopus is a mollusc.

questions.s: Echinoderms such as starfish are characterised by
o: a hard shell and a mantle
jointed legs and a hard cuticle
questions.e: Adult echinoderms have five-part radial symmetry and use tube feet powered by a water vascular system. Jointed legs belong to arthropods.

questions.s: Which of the following has a four-chambered heart?
questions.e: Crocodiles are unusual reptiles with a four-chambered heart. Frogs have three chambers, and sharks have two.

questions.s: Lichen is a symbiotic association between
o: a moss and a fern plant
questions.e: The fungus gives protection and water, while the photosynthetic partner supplies food. It is an example of mutualism.

questions.s: In an ecological pyramid of energy, the energy available at each higher trophic level
o: stays almost the same each time
questions.e: Most energy is lost as heat in respiration and in waste, so only about a tenth moves up. For this reason food chains are short.

questions.s: Which of the following food chains is correctly arranged?
questions.e: Arrows point from the food to the feeder, so energy flows from producer to primary, secondary and tertiary consumers.

questions.s: The process by which nitrogen gas is converted into nitrates in the soil by lightning and bacteria is part of the
questions.e: Nitrogen fixation, nitrification, assimilation, ammonification and denitrification make up the nitrogen cycle.

questions.s: Denitrifying bacteria
questions.e: Denitrification returns N₂ to the atmosphere. Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter oxidise ammonia to nitrite and nitrate.

questions.s: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
o: Absorption by the oceans and seas
questions.e: Respiration and combustion release CO₂. Photosynthesis removes it, and coal formation locks carbon away.

questions.s: Ecological succession that begins on bare rock is called
questions.e: Primary succession begins where no soil exists, with pioneer species such as lichens. Secondary succession starts on previously vegetated soil.

questions.s: The term 'niche' refers to
o: the food chain of its area
questions.e: The niche includes feeding, activity and interactions of a species. The place where it lives is its habitat.

questions.s: A plant growing in a desert and having reduced leaves, thick cuticle and deep roots is a
questions.e: Xerophytes are adapted to dry conditions by cutting down water loss. Hydrophytes live in water and halophytes in salty soil.

questions.s: Amoeba moves and feeds using
questions.e: Amoeba extends cytoplasmic projections called pseudopodia to move and to engulf food. Paramecium has cilia and Euglena has a flagellum.

questions.s: The Malaria parasite Plasmodium belongs to the kingdom
questions.e: Plasmodium is a unicellular eukaryote transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, so it is placed among protists.

questions.s: The Gram stain separates bacteria into two groups because of differences in their
questions.e: Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan wall that retains the crystal violet stain, but Gram-negative ones have a thin wall and an outer membrane.

questions.s: Roundworms (Ascaris) are placed in the phylum
questions.e: Nematodes are unsegmented, cylindrical worms with a complete digestive tract. Flatworms are flattened.

questions.s: Sponges (Porifera) obtain food by
questions.e: Choanocytes with flagella create a water current and trap food particles. Sponges have no true tissues or organs.

questions.s: Which of these is a warm-blooded vertebrate class?
questions.e: Birds and mammals maintain constant body temperature internally. Fish, amphibians and reptiles are cold-blooded.

questions.s: Which of the following plants reproduces by spores and has true roots, stems and leaves but no seeds?
questions.e: Ferns are pteridophytes with vascular tissue and spore-bearing leaves. Mosses lack true roots, and pine and rose make seeds.

questions.s: The biggest ecosystem comprising all living things on Earth and their environment is the
questions.e: The biosphere is the zone of life including land, water and air. A biome is a large region such as desert or tundra.

questions.s: Acid rain is formed mainly by the dissolution in rain water of
questions.e: These oxides, released from burning fuels, form sulphuric and nitric acids in the atmosphere, damaging plants and buildings.

questions.s: Depletion of the ozone layer is mainly caused by
questions.e: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere which destroy ozone. The ozone layer shields the Earth from ultraviolet rays.

questions.s: Overgrowth of algae in a pond due to excess fertiliser runoff is called
questions.e: Excess nutrients cause an algal bloom; when the algae die, bacteria use up oxygen and fish die. Biomagnification refers to toxins accumulating up food chains.

questions.s: A virus that infects bacteria is called a
questions.e: A bacteriophage has a head containing DNA and a tail used to inject it into a bacterium.

questions.s: In an aquatic food chain, DDT concentrations are highest in the
questions.e: A non-degradable pesticide accumulates and its concentration rises at each trophic level (biomagnification), reaching the highest value in top predators.

questions.s: Which kingdom contains multicellular, heterotrophic organisms without cell walls?
questions.e: Animal cells lack walls and animals ingest food. Fungi have chitin walls, and plants have cellulose walls.

questions.s: The population of rabbits in a field rises until limited by food. The upper limit that the environment can support is the
questions.e: The carrying capacity is the maximum population size sustained by resources. Biotic potential is the maximum reproductive capacity.

questions.s: A name written as Panthera leo persica shows that
o: it is a subspecies of Panthera leo
Panthera is the name of the species
persica is the name of the genus
leo is the name of the family
questions.e: A three-part name gives genus, species and subspecies, so persica is a subspecies of the lion, Panthera leo. The first word is always the genus.

questions.s: Which of the following pairs of organism and phylum is mismatched?
questions.e: Octopus is a mollusc, a cephalopod, not an echinoderm. The other pairs are correct.

questions.s: Which feature is used to separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes?
o: Presence of DNA in the cell
Presence of ribosomes in the cell
questions.e: Prokaryotes lack a nuclear envelope and membrane-bound organelles. All cells have DNA, ribosomes and a plasma membrane.

questions.s: In a food web, an organism feeding on both plants and animals is described as
questions.e: Omnivores feed at more than one trophic level, such as humans and crows. Herbivores eat only plants.

questions.s: Alternation of generations in plants means that
o: two diploid plants alternate in turn
growth alternates between day and night
male and female plants alternate in a field
questions.e: The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis, and the zygote forms the sporophyte, which makes spores by meiosis.

questions.s: The first trophic level in a grazing food chain in a pond is
questions.e: Phytoplankton are the producers; zooplankton feed on them as primary consumers.

questions.s: A pond contains 400 fish. Over a year, 60 are born, 20 die, 10 move in and 30 move out. The population at the end of the year is
questions.e: Change = births + immigration − deaths − emigration = 60 + 10 − 20 − 30 = 20, so 400 + 20 = 420.

questions.s: Competition between two different species for the same limited resource is
questions.e: Interspecific competition involves different species, while intraspecific involves members of the same species.

questions.s: Which structure in bacteria carries genes in addition to the main chromosome and can be passed between cells?
questions.e: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules, often carrying antibiotic resistance genes, and can transfer between bacteria.

questions.s: A tropical rain forest differs from a desert mainly in having
o: few species and very low rainfall
questions.e: A rain forest has abundant rainfall and a very large number of species. A desert has low rainfall and low diversity.

questions.s: The scientific name Mangifera indica refers to
questions.e: Mangifera indica is the binomial name of the mango, a dicot fruit tree widely grown in Sindh and Punjab.

questions.s: Mosses are mostly found in damp places because they
o: have deep roots to absorb water
have thick waxy leaves for storage
need water for sperms to swim
questions.e: Bryophytes depend on a film of water for fertilisation and lack true roots. They do make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.s: Tigers, lions and eagles occupy the ecological position of
questions.e: They feed on other animals, so they occupy higher trophic levels.

questions.s: A student finds an animal with a body covered with feathers, a beak, and forelimbs modified into wings. The animal belongs to
questions.e: Feathers and a beak with wings identify birds. Mammals have hair and reptiles have scales.

questions.s: Bacteria reproduce asexually mainly by
questions.e: A bacterial cell copies its DNA and divides into two. A spindle and mitosis are absent in prokaryotes.

questions.s: The cause of the disease cholera is a
questions.e: Vibrio cholerae spreads through contaminated water. It is a comma-shaped bacterium.

questions.s: Which of these correctly pairs a disease with its type of causative agent?
questions.e: Plasmodium is a protozoan. Tuberculosis is bacterial, influenza viral and ringworm is a fungal infection.

questions.s: Which of these organisms is a producer but is not a plant?
questions.e: Cyanobacteria carry out photosynthesis although they are prokaryotes in Monera. Amoeba, yeast and Hydra are heterotrophs.

questions.s: Mosquitoes, spiders and crabs all belong to the phylum
questions.e: Arthropods have jointed legs, a chitinous exoskeleton and segmented bodies. Molluscs have soft bodies, usually with a shell.

questions.s: Which of the following is a primary consumer?
questions.e: A primary consumer feeds directly on producers, so herbivores such as a goat fit. Eagles, tigers and snakes are carnivores.

questions.s: The relationship in which both organisms benefit is called
questions.e: Mutualism benefits both partners, as in lichens or root nodules. In parasitism, only one gains and the host is harmed.

questions.s: A flea living on a dog and feeding on its blood is an example of
questions.e: An ectoparasite lives on the body surface of the host and harms it. Endoparasites, such as tapeworms, live inside.

questions.s: Pioneer species in primary succession on bare rock are usually
questions.e: Lichens break down rock and add organic matter, forming the first soil. Trees come much later, in a climax community.

questions.s: Which of the following is a feature of all members of Kingdom Fungi?
questions.e: Fungal walls are made of chitin and they are heterotrophs. Cellulose walls occur in plants.

questions.s: Which of the following is an arthropod class that has three pairs of walking legs?
questions.e: Insects have three pairs of legs, with a head, thorax and abdomen. Arachnids have four pairs of legs.

questions.s: The number of legs of a spider is
questions.e: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs and two body regions, the cephalothorax and abdomen. Six legs are for insects.

questions.s: If 10,000 J of energy is stored by producers, how much is expected to reach the secondary consumers according to the ten per cent rule?
questions.e: Primary consumers receive 10 % of 10,000 J, which is 1,000 J, and secondary consumers receive 10 % of that, which is 100 J.

questions.s: Which of these is not a function of the kingdom Fungi in the ecosystem?
questions.e: Fungi lack chlorophyll and so cannot photosynthesise. They decompose dead matter and form mycorrhiza with roots.

questions.s: In which part of the alimentary canal does the digestion of starch begin?
questions.e: Salivary amylase starts breaking starch into maltose in the mouth. Stomach acid stops its action, and pancreatic amylase completes digestion later.

questions.s: Which enzyme in gastric juice digests proteins?
questions.e: Pepsin, activated from pepsinogen by hydrochloric acid, acts at pH about 2 in the stomach. Trypsin works in the small intestine.

questions.s: Most absorption of digested food takes place in the
questions.e: The small intestine has villi and microvilli that give a huge surface area. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.

questions.s: Bile is produced by the
questions.e: The liver makes bile and the gall bladder only stores and concentrates it. Bile emulsifies fats and has no digestive enzymes.

questions.s: The main function of the large intestine is to
questions.e: The colon absorbs water and salts from undigested residue. Protein digestion and amino acid uptake occur earlier in the tract.

questions.s: Which of the following secretions has no digestive enzyme but helps in fat digestion?
questions.e: Bile salts emulsify fat into small droplets and so increase surface area for lipase. Pancreatic and gastric juices contain enzymes.

questions.s: Trypsinogen secreted by the pancreas is activated in the duodenum by
questions.e: Enterokinase from the intestinal wall converts inactive trypsinogen to trypsin, which prevents the pancreas from digesting itself. Ptyalin is salivary amylase.

questions.s: The final products of protein digestion are
questions.e: Proteases and peptidases break proteins to amino acids, which are absorbed by villi. Peptones are only intermediate products.

questions.s: Which structure in the small intestine absorbs fatty acids and glycerol into the lymph?
questions.e: Each villus contains a lacteal, a lymph vessel which carries absorbed fats. Glucose and amino acids enter blood capillaries.

questions.s: The pancreas secretes an enzyme that digests fat. It is
questions.e: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyses triglycerides to fatty acids and glycerol in the duodenum.

questions.s: Peristalsis in the oesophagus is
o: secretion of mucus in the stomach
questions.e: Alternate contraction and relaxation of circular and longitudinal muscle moves the bolus down; it is mechanical, not chemical.

questions.s: Which of the following correctly pairs an enzyme with its site of action?
questions.e: Trypsin acts in the duodenum at alkaline pH. Pepsin works in the stomach, and salivary amylase works in the mouth.

questions.s: Vitamin K, needed for blood clotting, is partly made by
questions.e: Intestinal flora produce vitamin K, which is absorbed through the colon. A lack of it delays clotting.

questions.s: The human heart has
questions.e: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles. Fish have two chambers, and amphibians have three.

questions.s: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.e: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. It is the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood in the adult.

questions.s: The red pigment haemoglobin in red blood cells carries
questions.e: Haemoglobin contains iron in haem groups that bind oxygen. Antibodies are transported in plasma.

questions.s: Which blood cells help in clotting of blood?
questions.e: Platelets (thrombocytes) release factors that start the clotting cascade. Lymphocytes are immune cells.

questions.s: The largest artery in the human body is the
questions.e: The aorta leaves the left ventricle and delivers oxygenated blood to the body. The vena cava is the largest vein.

questions.s: The blood group whose red cells carry the A antigen as well as the B antigen is
questions.e: AB has both antigens and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal recipient. O has no antigens.

questions.s: The valve between the left atrium and left ventricle is the
questions.e: The bicuspid (mitral) valve has two flaps and stops backflow into the left atrium. The tricuspid valve is on the right side.

questions.s: Which of the following is true about veins?
o: They have valves and return blood
They carry blood at high pressure
questions.e: Veins have thin walls and valves to prevent backflow. The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

questions.s: Group O negative red cells are called universal donor cells because they can generally be given to people of
o: only Rh-negative people of group A
questions.e: O negative red cells have no A, B or Rh antigens, so they are the universal donor type.

questions.s: The Rh factor is a cause of danger to a second baby when
o: an Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative foetus
an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus
questions.e: The mother's first exposure to Rh-positive blood at birth produces antibodies, which can attack later Rh-positive foetuses.

questions.s: White blood cells that engulf germs by phagocytosis include
questions.e: Neutrophils and monocytes (macrophages) are phagocytes. Plasma cells make antibodies.

questions.s: The closing of the atrioventricular valves produces the sound
questions.e: The AV valves close at the start of ventricular systole giving 'lub'. The semilunar valves closing gives 'dub'.

questions.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of blood plasma?
questions.e: Red cells are blood cells, not plasma. Plasma is about 90 % water with proteins such as albumin and fibrinogen, and wastes like urea.

questions.s: The exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the
questions.e: Alveoli are thin-walled air sacs surrounded by capillaries, so gas exchange is fast by diffusion.

questions.s: The muscle that contracts and moves downward during inhalation is the
questions.e: When the diaphragm contracts and flattens, the chest volume increases and air rushes in.

questions.s: Which gas is carried mostly as bicarbonate ions in blood plasma?
questions.e: About 70 % of CO₂ is transported as bicarbonate formed by carbonic anhydrase in red cells.

questions.s: Air passes from the nose to the lungs through the
questions.e: The trachea, supported by C-shaped cartilage rings, leads to the bronchi. The oesophagus carries food.

questions.s: Which gas combines with haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen does?
questions.e: Carbon monoxide forms carboxyhaemoglobin, which reduces oxygen carriage and causes poisoning.

questions.s: The amount of air breathed in and out during normal quiet breathing is the
questions.e: Tidal volume is about 500 mL. Vital capacity is the maximum volume that can be exhaled after the deepest inhalation.

questions.s: Which structure prevents food from entering the trachea during swallowing?
questions.e: The epiglottis covers the glottis during swallowing. The uvula is at the back of the soft palate.

questions.s: Smoking increases the risk of lung damage because tar
o: increases the surface area of alveoli
questions.e: Cilia normally sweep mucus and dust upwards; when they are damaged, mucus and germs stay in the lungs, leading to bronchitis and cancer.

questions.s: A person's tidal volume is 500 mL and breathing rate is 15 per minute. Of each breath, 150 mL stays in the dead space. The alveolar ventilation per minute is
questions.e: Alveolar ventilation = (500 − 150) × 15 = 350 × 15 = 5,250 mL. The value 7,500 mL is the total minute volume, which includes dead space.

questions.s: The Bohr effect describes the fact that haemoglobin
o: binds more oxygen when CO₂ is high
releases oxygen only at a high pH
is not affected by carbon dioxide
releases more oxygen when CO₂ is high
questions.e: A rise in CO₂ lowers pH and shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the right, so tissues receive more oxygen.

questions.s: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.e: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter blood and form urine.

questions.s: The main nitrogenous waste of humans is
questions.e: The liver converts toxic ammonia to urea, which the kidneys excrete. Birds excrete uric acid.

questions.s: Urine is stored in the
questions.e: The bladder stores urine and the urethra carries it out of the body. The ureters carry it from kidneys to bladder.

questions.s: Ultrafiltration of blood in the kidney occurs in the
questions.e: High pressure in the glomerulus forces water, glucose, salts and urea into the capsule. Cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

questions.s: In a healthy person, glucose is completely reabsorbed in the
questions.e: All the filtered glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed by active transport in the proximal tubule. Glucose in urine suggests diabetes.

questions.s: The countercurrent mechanism in the loop of Henle helps the kidney to
questions.e: The loop creates a salt gradient in the medulla, which allows water to be drawn out in the collecting duct.

questions.s: A patient's urine contains protein. The most likely cause is damage to the
questions.e: Large proteins normally cannot pass the filtration membrane; their presence points to damage of the glomerulus.

questions.s: The basic unit of the nervous system is the
questions.e: A neuron is a nerve cell which carries impulses; nephrons are in the kidney.

questions.s: The part of the brain that controls balance and coordination of movement is the
questions.e: The cerebellum coordinates posture and smooth muscle action. The cerebrum controls thought and voluntary action.

questions.s: The brain and the spinal cord form the
questions.e: The CNS integrates information. Nerves outside it make up the peripheral system.

questions.s: The part of a neuron that carries the impulse away from the cell body is the
questions.e: An axon conducts impulses away; dendrites receive impulses towards the cell body.

questions.s: A reflex action is controlled mainly by the
questions.e: In a spinal reflex arc the impulse goes from receptor to sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron and effector without waiting for the brain.

questions.s: Which chemical is released at a synapse to transmit an impulse?
questions.e: When an impulse reaches the terminal, vesicles release neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft.

questions.s: The myelin sheath around an axon
questions.e: Myelin insulates the axon so the impulse jumps between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction).

questions.s: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is about
questions.e: The sodium-potassium pump and leakier potassium channels keep the inside negative relative to the outside.

questions.s: During an action potential, depolarisation is mainly due to the entry of
questions.e: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open and Na⁺ rushes in. Repolarisation follows as K⁺ moves out.

questions.s: Which part of the eye contains the light-sensitive cells?
questions.e: The retina has rods for dim light and cones for colour. The iris controls pupil size.

questions.s: A person who cannot see well in dim light is likely to be deficient in vitamin
questions.e: Vitamin A is needed to make rhodopsin in rod cells. Its deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.s: In short-sightedness (myopia), the image is formed
o: on the yellow spot of retina
questions.e: The eyeball is too long or the lens too strong, so rays focus before the retina. A concave lens corrects it.

questions.s: The autonomic nervous system differs from the somatic nervous system in that it
o: is part of the CNS only
questions.e: The autonomic system has sympathetic and parasympathetic parts controlling smooth and cardiac muscle and glands.

questions.s: The hormone that controls the level of sugar in blood and is made by the pancreas is
questions.e: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting uptake and storage as glycogen.

questions.s: The 'master gland' of the body is the
questions.e: The pituitary controls many other endocrine glands through its hormones.

questions.s: Lack of iodine in the diet causes enlargement of the thyroid called
questions.e: The thyroid needs iodine to make thyroxine, and without it, it enlarges.

questions.s: The hormone adrenaline prepares the body for
questions.e: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla raises heart rate, glucose in blood and blood flow to the muscles.

questions.s: Which hormone raises blood glucose by breaking glycogen in the liver?
questions.e: Glucagon from alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans raises blood sugar. Insulin does the opposite.

questions.s: Diabetes mellitus is caused by
o: lack or poor action of insulin
questions.e: High blood glucose results when insulin is insufficient or cells do not respond; glucose then appears in urine.

questions.s: Excess growth hormone in an adult causes
questions.e: After growth plates close, excess hormone enlarges hands, feet and jaw. Gigantism arises if the excess occurs in childhood.

questions.s: The hormone that regulates the metabolic rate of the body is
questions.e: Thyroxine from the thyroid increases the rate of oxidation in cells and affects growth.

questions.s: Negative feedback in hormone control means that
o: its effect increases its own release
its effect reduces its own release
hormones are never controlled by the body
hormones act only on the gland making them
questions.e: Negative feedback restores balance, for example high blood glucose raises insulin, which lowers glucose and then reduces insulin release.

questions.s: Oxytocin, which causes uterine contractions during childbirth, is released from the
questions.e: Oxytocin and ADH are made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.s: Vaccination protects against a disease by
o: killing all germs in the blood
removing the white cells from blood
questions.e: A vaccine contains weakened or killed pathogens or their antigens, giving active immunity and memory cells.

questions.s: Which of these is a viral disease?
questions.e: Poliomyelitis is caused by poliovirus. Cholera, tuberculosis and typhoid are bacterial.

questions.s: Antibodies are made by
questions.e: On activation, B cells form plasma cells which secrete antibodies against a specific antigen.

questions.s: Immunity acquired by a baby through mother's milk is
questions.e: The baby receives ready-made antibodies without producing them itself, so protection is temporary.

questions.s: The anti-tetanus serum given after a deep wound gives
questions.e: Serum contains ready-made antibodies and acts quickly but lasts only a short time.

questions.s: Which organ is a primary lymphoid organ where T cells mature?
questions.e: T lymphocytes mature in the thymus. B cells mature in bone marrow.

questions.s: HIV mainly attacks
questions.e: HIV destroys CD4 helper T cells, weakening the entire immune response and leading to AIDS.

questions.s: A substance that stimulates the body to produce antibodies is a(n)
questions.e: An antigen is a foreign molecule recognised by lymphocytes. Antibiotics are drugs that kill or inhibit bacteria.

questions.s: Why are antibiotics ineffective against influenza?
o: Influenza bacteria are resistant to all drugs
Influenza is caused by a virus, not bacteria
Antibiotics are destroyed by the stomach in all cases
Influenza is caused by a fungus in the lungs
questions.e: Antibiotics act on bacterial processes such as cell wall synthesis, but viruses reproduce inside host cells.

questions.s: A second exposure to the same pathogen gives a faster and stronger response mainly due to
questions.e: Memory B and T cells formed in the first response recognise the antigen quickly.

questions.s: Fertilisation in humans normally takes place in the
questions.e: The sperm meets the ovum in the upper part of the oviduct. The embryo later implants in the uterus.

questions.s: The female gamete is called the
questions.e: The ovum is produced in the ovary; the zygote forms after fertilisation.

questions.s: The hormone responsible for the development of male secondary sexual characters is
questions.e: Testosterone from the Leydig cells of the testes produces deep voice and facial hair.

questions.s: Ovulation in the menstrual cycle is triggered by a surge of
questions.e: A midcycle LH surge causes the mature follicle to release the egg.

questions.s: The placenta
o: mixes the blood of mother and foetus
questions.e: Substances diffuse across the placenta, but the two blood supplies do not mix.

questions.s: Menstruation occurs when
o: progesterone falls and the lining is shed
ovulation takes place in an ovary
progesterone rises sharply in the blood
questions.e: If there is no pregnancy, the corpus luteum degenerates, so progesterone falls and the lining is shed.

questions.s: The corpus luteum secretes
questions.e: After ovulation the empty follicle forms the corpus luteum, which makes progesterone to maintain the uterine lining.

questions.s: Meiosis during spermatogenesis produces from one primary spermatocyte
questions.e: One diploid cell gives four haploid spermatids that become sperms. In oogenesis, only one ovum results.

questions.s: The normal diploid number of chromosomes in a human body cell is 46. The number in a sperm is
questions.e: Meiosis halves the number so that the sperm has 23 chromosomes, and fusion with the egg restores 46.

questions.s: The longest bone in the human body is the
questions.e: The femur in the thigh is the longest and strongest bone.

questions.s: Which protein filaments slide over each other during muscle contraction?
questions.e: In the sliding filament theory, myosin heads pull actin filaments inwards, shortening the sarcomere using ATP.

questions.s: Lactic acid builds up in muscles during strenuous exercise because
o: glucose is broken down without oxygen
there is too much oxygen present
questions.e: Anaerobic respiration converts pyruvate to lactic acid when oxygen supply is inadequate, causing fatigue.

questions.s: Deficiency of vitamin D in children causes
questions.e: Without vitamin D, calcium absorption is poor and bones become soft and bent. Scurvy is due to lack of vitamin C.

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement about the heart.
o: The left ventricle pumps blood to the body
The right ventricle has a thicker wall
The atria receive blood from the veins
questions.e: The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood at high pressure around the body, while the right pumps to the lungs only.

questions.s: The sinoatrial node in the right atrium
questions.e: The SA node generates impulses that start each heartbeat. Pumping is done by the ventricles.

questions.s: A heartbeat of 72 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 mL give a cardiac output of about
questions.e: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume = 72 × 70 = 5,040 mL per minute, which is about 5.0 L per minute.

questions.s: During inhalation, the volume of the thoracic cavity
o: stays the same and pressure rises
questions.e: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles enlarges the cavity, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air enters.

questions.s: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) acts on the kidney to
questions.e: ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable to water, giving a smaller volume of concentrated urine.

questions.s: The correct sequence of a reflex arc is
o: receptor, sensory neuron, relay neuron, motor neuron, effector
receptor, motor neuron, relay neuron, sensory neuron, effector
effector, sensory neuron, relay neuron, motor neuron, receptor
receptor, relay neuron, sensory neuron, effector, motor neuron
questions.e: The impulse enters the spinal cord through a sensory neuron, passes a relay neuron and leaves through a motor neuron to the effector.

questions.s: Sperms are produced in the
questions.e: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The epididymis stores sperm.

questions.s: A woman's menstrual cycle is regular, 28 days long. Ovulation is expected on about day
questions.e: Ovulation occurs about 14 days before the next menstruation, so on day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

questions.s: Bones are joined to muscles by
questions.e: Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone.

questions.s: Which type of joint allows movement in all directions, as in the shoulder?
questions.e: A ball and socket joint allows rotation and movement in several planes. A hinge joint moves in one plane only.

questions.s: Which one of the following diseases is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C?
questions.e: Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation, and a lack leads to bleeding gums. Beriberi is from lack of thiamine.

questions.s: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.e: Mendel worked on garden peas and discovered the basic laws of inheritance. Morgan worked on Drosophila and Watson co-discovered the DNA structure.

questions.s: The organism used by Mendel in his experiments was the
questions.e: Mendel used Pisum sativum because it has clear contrasting traits, a short life cycle and can be self- or cross-pollinated.

questions.s: An allele that masks the effect of another allele in a heterozygote is
questions.e: A dominant allele hides the recessive allele when the two occur together. Codominant alleles are both expressed, so neither is masked.

questions.s: A cross between two individuals differing in one pair of contrasting characters is a
questions.e: A monohybrid cross follows one gene, such as tall × dwarf. A dihybrid cross follows two genes.

questions.s: A person with blood group O has the genotype
questions.e: Group O is recessive and requires two i alleles. IAi gives group A and IBi gives group B.

questions.s: The scientist who proposed the double helix model of DNA with Watson was
questions.e: Watson and Crick built the model in 1953 from X-ray data and Chargaff's rules. Franklin provided the X-ray photographs.

questions.s: The sex chromosomes of a human male are
questions.e: Males have one X and one Y chromosome. Females have XX.

questions.s: The father of a child determines the sex of the child because
o: his sperms carry either X or Y
he always gives an X chromosome
only the mother's chromosomes decide sex
he always gives two Y chromosomes
questions.e: Males make X-bearing and Y-bearing sperms in equal numbers, whereas all eggs carry X. The sperm that fertilises decides the sex.

questions.s: The term used for changes in the DNA sequence of a gene is
questions.e: A mutation alters the nucleotide sequence. Transcription and translation are steps of protein synthesis.

questions.s: Down syndrome is caused by
questions.e: Trisomy 21 gives a person 47 chromosomes. Turner syndrome is XO.

questions.s: Charles Darwin explained evolution by
questions.e: Darwin proposed that variations exist, more offspring are born than survive, and the fittest survive and reproduce. Use and disuse is Lamarck's idea.

questions.s: The remains or traces of ancient organisms preserved in rocks are called
questions.e: Fossils give evidence of past life and show how organisms have changed over time.

questions.s: Enzymes that cut DNA at specific sites are called
questions.e: Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors in genetic engineering. DNA ligase joins fragments.

questions.s: The structure of a gene is made of
questions.e: A gene is a segment of DNA, and it codes for a polypeptide or RNA.

questions.s: A trait that is controlled by genes on the X chromosome is described as
questions.e: X-linked traits such as colour blindness and haemophilia show a different pattern of inheritance in males and females.

questions.s: Haemophilia is a disorder in which
o: the pancreas fails to make insulin
the colour of skin is lost
questions.e: Lack of a clotting factor causes prolonged bleeding. It is an X-linked recessive disease.

questions.s: In a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt), the percentage of dwarf offspring expected is
questions.e: The cross gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so one quarter are tt (dwarf). Three quarters are tall.

questions.s: The phenotypic ratio of the F₂ generation in a monohybrid cross with complete dominance is
questions.e: Selfing Tt F₁ plants gives 3 tall to 1 dwarf. The genotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.s: The phenotypic ratio in the F₂ of a dihybrid cross is
questions.e: Two genes assorting independently give four phenotypes in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, from the 16 combinations.

questions.s: In a cross AaBb × AaBb, the probability that an offspring is aabb is
questions.e: Probability of aa is ¼ and of bb is ¼, so aabb = ¼ × ¼ = 1/16, from independent assortment.

questions.s: In a cross AaBb × AaBb, the fraction of offspring showing both dominant phenotypes is
questions.e: The chance of A_ is ¾ and of B_ is ¾, so A_B_ = 9/16. The fraction 3/16 is for one dominant and one recessive trait.

questions.s: A test cross is made between an individual of dominant phenotype and
o: a heterozygous plant of any kind
questions.e: Crossing with aa shows whether the unknown is AA (all dominant) or Aa (1 : 1 ratio).

questions.s: A test cross of a tall pea plant gives 52 tall and 48 dwarf offspring. The tall plant is
questions.e: A ratio near 1 : 1 shows that the tall parent made two kinds of gametes, so it is heterozygous.

questions.s: When red-flowered and white-flowered snapdragons are crossed, all F₁ plants are pink. This is an example of
questions.e: Neither allele completely masks the other, giving an intermediate phenotype. The F₂ ratio is 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white.

questions.s: The AB blood group is an example of
questions.e: Both IA and IB alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote, so red cells carry both antigens.

questions.s: A man of blood group A (IAi) marries a woman of blood group B (IBi). The probability that their child has group O is
questions.e: The cross IAi × IBi gives IAIB, IAi, IBi and ii in equal proportions, so ii (group O) is one in four.

questions.s: A man with group AB marries a woman with group O. Their children can have only the blood groups
questions.e: IAIB × ii gives IAi and IBi, so each child is A or B. None can be AB or O.

questions.s: A colour-blind man (XcY) marries a woman with normal vision who is not a carrier (XCXC). Their sons will be
questions.e: Sons receive Y from the father and an XC from the mother, so they are normal. Daughters are carriers.

questions.s: A carrier mother (XCXc) and a normal father (XCY) have a daughter. The chance that she is colour-blind is
questions.e: The daughter receives XC from her father, so she cannot be colour-blind though she may be a carrier.

questions.s: According to Chargaff's rule, in a double-stranded DNA molecule
o: the amount of adenine equals that of guanine
the amount of thymine equals that of cytosine
the amount of adenine equals that of thymine
questions.e: A pairs with T and G with C, so A = T and G = C, and total purines equal total pyrimidines.

questions.s: A DNA sample has 28 % adenine. The percentage of guanine is
questions.e: A = T = 28 %, so A + T = 56 %. The remaining 44 % is split between G and C, which gives 22 % each.

questions.s: DNA replication is described as semi-conservative because
o: both strands of a daughter are new
each daughter has one old strand
half of the DNA is not copied
questions.e: The Meselson–Stahl experiment showed that every daughter helix keeps one parental strand.

questions.s: The enzyme that joins nucleotides to build a new DNA strand is
questions.e: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to the 3′ end of the growing chain. Helicase unwinds the helix.

questions.s: The template strand of DNA reads TAC GGA. The corresponding mRNA codons are
questions.e: mRNA is complementary to the template: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C. So TAC becomes AUG and GGA becomes CCU. RNA has U, not T.

questions.s: The process of making mRNA from a DNA template is
questions.e: Transcription is done by RNA polymerase in the nucleus. Translation occurs on ribosomes.

questions.s: The codon AUG codes for
questions.e: AUG begins translation and codes for methionine. UAA, UAG and UGA are the stop codons.

questions.s: The genetic code is said to be degenerate because
o: most amino acids have several codons
every codon codes for several amino acids
some codons code for no amino acid
the code differs in each species
questions.e: There are 64 codons but only 20 amino acids, so several codons code for the same amino acid.

questions.s: Sickle cell anaemia results from
o: an extra chromosome in the cell
a missing X chromosome in females
one base change in a haemoglobin gene
an infection by a blood parasite
questions.e: Substitution of one base changes glutamic acid to valine in the β chain, so haemoglobin forms fibres in low oxygen.

questions.s: A person with Turner syndrome has the chromosome constitution
questions.e: Turner syndrome is XO monosomy in females, giving 45 chromosomes. Klinefelter syndrome is XXY.

questions.s: The technique used to make many copies of a segment of DNA in a test tube is
questions.e: PCR uses repeated heating and cooling cycles with Taq polymerase to amplify DNA exponentially.

questions.s: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to their
questions.e: Negatively charged DNA moves toward the positive electrode and smaller fragments travel further through the gel.

questions.s: A plasmid is used in genetic engineering as a
o: vector for a gene in bacteria
questions.e: A plasmid is a small circular DNA that can carry a foreign gene into a host cell and be copied.

questions.s: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell, produced in 1996, was a sheep named
questions.e: Dolly was produced by nuclear transfer from an adult udder cell into an enucleated egg.

questions.s: Homologous organs, such as the forelimb of a bat and the human arm, show
questions.e: They share the same basic bone plan, which suggests descent from a common ancestor, in spite of the different uses.

questions.s: Lamarck proposed that
o: characters acquired during life are inherited
all organisms arise from spontaneous generation
questions.e: Lamarckism, 'inheritance of acquired characters', has been rejected, as changes in body cells do not alter the gametes.

questions.s: The peppered moth became mostly dark near industrial areas in England because
o: moths changed colour to match their surroundings
soot caused mutations in the moths
dark moths were less visible to predators
light moths migrated away in a body
questions.e: This is an example of natural selection: predators ate more of the conspicuous light moths so dark moths survived and reproduced.

questions.s: Bacteria become resistant to an antibiotic mostly because
o: the drug causes bacteria to want resistance
the bacteria learn to avoid the drug
the antibiotic changes bacterial DNA to resist it
questions.e: Selection by the antibiotic favours rare resistant mutants, which multiply, so misuse of antibiotics spreads resistance.

questions.s: Two heterozygous parents with the genotype AaBb produce 160 offspring. The expected number with the genotype aabb is
questions.e: The probability of aabb is 1/16, so 160 × 1/16 = 10. The value 30 would apply to a class with probability 3/16.

questions.s: A cross AaBb × aabb is carried out. The expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is
questions.e: AaBb makes four gamete types in equal numbers, and aabb makes only ab, so the four phenotypes are equally likely.

questions.s: How many different types of gametes can be formed by a plant with the genotype AaBbCc?
questions.e: Each heterozygous locus doubles the number of gamete types, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

questions.s: A pea plant Tt is self-pollinated and gives 800 seeds. The expected number of dwarf plants is
questions.e: Dwarf plants are tt, one quarter of the offspring, so 800 ÷ 4 = 200. The 600 is for tall plants.

questions.s: A woman of group A whose mother was group O marries a man of group B whose father was group O. The probability that their first child is group O is
questions.e: The woman must be IAi because she received i from her mother, and the man is IBi. The cross gives ii in 1/4 of children.

questions.s: A colour-blind woman (XcXc) marries a man with normal vision (XCY). Their children will be
o: all sons normal, all daughters colour-blind
half of the sons and daughters colour-blind
all sons affected, all daughters carriers
all sons and daughters normal in vision
questions.e: Sons get Y and an Xc, so they are colour-blind. Daughters get XC and an Xc, so they are carriers with normal vision.

questions.s: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 4 % of people have a recessive condition (q² = 0.04). The percentage of carriers is
questions.e: q = √0.04 = 0.2, p = 0.8, and carriers = 2pq = 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.32. The value 64 % is p², the homozygous dominant class, and 20 % is q itself.

questions.s: In a Hardy–Weinberg population, the frequency of allele a is 0.3. The expected frequency of the genotype Aa is
questions.e: p = 0.7 and q = 0.3, so 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42. The values 0.09 and 0.49 are q² and p².

questions.s: Which of the following would NOT disturb the Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
o: Random mating in a very large population
Migration of individuals into the population
Mutation of one allele to another
questions.e: The equilibrium assumes random mating, a large population, no migration, no mutation and no selection. Gene flow, selection and mutation each change allele frequencies.

questions.s: Meiosis helps to maintain the chromosome number in sexually reproducing organisms because it
o: makes cells identical to the parent
happens in all the body cells
questions.e: Gametes are haploid, and fertilisation restores the diploid number.

questions.s: Which statement describes crossing over?
o: Separation of sister chromatids in anaphase II
Duplication of DNA in the S phase
Joining of two gametes at fertilisation
Exchange of segments in prophase I
questions.e: Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, producing new combinations of alleles.

questions.s: During translation, the anticodon is found on
questions.e: A tRNA's anticodon pairs with the codon on mRNA, delivering the matching amino acid at the ribosome.

questions.s: Which of the following is an example of a genetically modified (GM) crop developed for improved nutrition?
o: Golden rice rich in provitamin A
questions.e: Golden rice contains genes that make β-carotene in the grain. The others involve breeding or farm practices, not gene transfer.

questions.s: The genetic make-up of an organism is its
questions.e: Genotype is the set of alleles, whereas phenotype is the visible expression.

questions.s: Which of the following bases is found only in RNA?
questions.e: RNA contains A, U, G and C. Thymine is replaced by uracil.

questions.s: A clone is a group of organisms that are
questions.e: Clones arise from asexual reproduction or artificial cloning and have the same DNA.

questions.s: Insulin for diabetic patients is now produced on a large scale using
questions.e: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria such as E. coli, which then make human insulin. It is safer than animal insulin.

questions.s: A Bt cotton plant is resistant to bollworm because it
o: has a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
questions.e: The Bt gene produces a protein toxic to certain insect larvae. It is an example of a genetically modified crop.

questions.s: A carrier woman (XCXc) marries a man with normal vision (XCY). The probability that a son is colour-blind is
questions.e: The sons get Y from the father and either XC or Xc from the mother with equal chance. The chance that a son is affected is ½.

questions.s: Why are X-linked recessive disorders more common in males?
o: Males have only one X chromosome
The Y chromosome carries the allele
questions.e: A single recessive allele on the X is expressed in a male as there is no second allele to mask it.

questions.s: A part of an mRNA of 90 nucleotides excluding the stop codon will code for how many amino acids?
questions.e: Each codon has three nucleotides and codes for one amino acid, so 90 ÷ 3 = 30.

questions.s: The wings of a bird and an insect are called analogous organs because
o: they have the same origin and structure
they are both vestigial in animals
they are made from the same bones
they have the same function, different origin
questions.e: Analogous organs result from convergent evolution and do not indicate close relationship.

questions.s: The theory of the origin of life stating that simple organic molecules were formed from gases on the early Earth was supported by the experiment of
questions.e: Miller and Urey passed electric sparks through methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour and obtained amino acids. Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation.
